issues.description: Using '// @ts-ignore' suppresses all TypeScript type checking for the import statement. This defeats the purpose of using TypeScript and hides potential type safety issues.
issues.suggestion: Either use proper TypeScript types for the NeverChangeDB module or install and use the official type definitions. If the library doesn't have types, consider '@ts-expect-error' with a specific reason comment, or improve the library integration.

issues.description: Global mutable state 'db' is declared with type 'any' and stored at module level. This creates a singleton pattern without proper encapsulation and makes the module harder to test, as state persists across test runs.
issues.suggestion: Encapsulate db state within a class or use a proper module pattern. Consider dependency injection for better testability. Create a getDb() helper function.

issues.description: Type annotation is 'any', which removes all type safety benefits. This should be properly typed with the actual NeverChangeDB type.
issues.suggestion: Replace 'let db: any = null' with 'let db: DBInstance | null = null' using proper type from the neverchange library.

issues.description: Logic error: 'if(db) db;' does nothing. The statement evaluates db but doesn't return or perform any action. The function continues to reinitialize the database even if it's already initialized, which could cause race conditions or multiple initialization attempts.
issues.suggestion: Change to 'if(db) return;' or 'if(db) return db;' to prevent re-initialization on subsequent calls.

issues.description: Parameter 'db' in migration up() function shadows the outer 'db' variable, creating confusion about scope and reference.
issues.suggestion: Rename the parameter to avoid shadowing, e.g., 'up: async (database: DBInstance) => {...}'

issues.description: Parameter 'db' in migration up() function shadows the outer 'db' variable, creating confusion about scope and reference.
issues.suggestion: Rename the parameter to avoid shadowing, e.g., 'up: async (database: DBInstance) => {...}'

issues.description: Function addTodo() does not validate input. The 'text' parameter is not checked for null, undefined, or empty strings before being inserted into the database.
issues.suggestion: Add validation at the start: if (!text || text.trim() === '') { throw new Error('Text cannot be empty'); }

issues.description: Error is caught but not re-thrown in addTodo(). The function silently fails, which could lead to data inconsistency and makes debugging harder. The caller has no way to know if the operation failed.
issues.suggestion: Either re-throw the error (like in updateTodo and deleteTodo) or return a result object indicating success/failure. This breaks the error handling pattern.

issues.description: Using console.log for success messages in production code. This creates noise in logs and should be replaced with proper logging framework.
issues.suggestion: Replace console.log with a proper logger instance (e.g., Winston, Pino, or the application's configured logger).

issues.description: No error handling in getTodos(). If db.query() throws an exception, it will propagate uncaught. Inconsistent with other functions that have try-catch.
issues.suggestion: Add try-catch block or document that this function throws errors, keeping consistency across the module.

issues.description: Function toggleTodo() has no input validation for the 'id' parameter. Negative, zero, or invalid IDs are not checked before executing the query.
issues.suggestion: Add validation: if (typeof id !== 'number' || id <= 0) { throw new Error('Invalid todo id'); }

issues.description: Function toggleTodo() has no error handling. If db.execute() fails, the error propagates uncaught. Inconsistent with updateTodo and deleteTodo which have try-catch.
issues.suggestion: Add try-catch block to match the error handling pattern used in other mutation functions.

issues.description: Function updateTodo() does not validate the 'text' parameter. Empty or null text could be inserted.
issues.suggestion: Add validation: if (!text || text.trim() === '') { throw new Error('Text cannot be empty'); }

issues.description: Function updateTodo() does not validate the 'id' parameter. Negative, zero, or invalid IDs are not checked.
issues.suggestion: Add validation: if (typeof id !== 'number' || id <= 0) { throw new Error('Invalid todo id'); }

issues.description: Using console.log for success messages in production code.
Function deleteTodo() does not validate the 'id' parameter. Negative, zero, or invalid IDs are not checked.
issues.suggestion: Add validation: if (typeof id !== 'number' || id <= 0) { throw new Error('Invalid todo id'); }

issues.description: Using console.log for success messages in production code.
No initialization check guard in exported functions. If initDb() is not called before using other functions, 'db' will be null and cause runtime errors (NullPointerException equivalent).
issues.suggestion: Add a helper function to check initialization: function ensureDbInitialized() { if (!db) throw new Error('Database not initialized. Call initDb() first.'); } and call it at the start of each exported function.

issues.description: No type exports or interfaces. The functions operate on generic 'any' types from the neverchange library, making it difficult for consumers to understand the expected API.
issues.suggestion: Export clear interfaces/types for database operations, e.g., 'export interface Todo { id: number; text: string; completed: boolean; deleted: boolean; }'

codeQuality.summary: The refactored db.ts file has significant code quality issues. Critical issue: logic error in initDb() at line 9 ('if(db) db;' does nothing). High-severity issues: @ts-ignore bypassing TypeScript safety, global mutable state without encapsulation, no initialization guards in exported functions. Medium-severity issues: inconsistent error handling (addTodo silently fails, toggleTodo propagates errors), missing input validation for all parameters, missing error handling in getTodos(). While SQL injection is prevented through parameterized queries, the lack of validation and error handling consistency presents maintainability and reliability concerns.

testCoverage.summary: The src/db.ts module has ZERO test coverage. No test files exist in the repository. All six exported functions lack any test coverage. Critical issues include: (1) Logic error 'if(db) db;' returns undefined instead of db - causes re-initialization; (2) No error handling in getTodos(); (3) No validation of input parameters; (4) No tests for database connection failures; (5) No edge case tests for empty strings, null values, non-existent IDs; (6) No integration tests verifying soft-delete, completed toggle, query filtering. Priority: Create comprehensive test suite with 40+ test cases covering initialization, CRUD operations, error paths, edge cases, and the critical initDb() bug.

suggestions.description: Early return pattern is broken. 'if(db) db;' does nothing - should use early return guard to prevent re-initialization.
suggestions.before:
export async function initDb() {

suggestions.after:

  if(db) return;
suggestions.benefits: Fixes broken logic, prevents re-initialization on subsequent calls, eliminates race conditions, improves code clarity.

refactorings.summary: The refactored src/db.ts file has solid structure but exhibits several refactoring opportunities that would significantly improve maintainability and reliability. Priority issues: (1) Fix the broken early-return logic in initDb() (line 9), (2) Extract reusable error handling wrapper to eliminate duplication, (3) Create getDb() helper to ensure database initialization and improve type safety, (4) Extract MIGRATIONS constant for better organization, (5) Replace @ts-ignore with proper TypeScript types. The highest-impact changes are fixing the initDb() bug and extracting the error handling pattern which appears 3+ times. These improvements would increase reliability, maintainability, and consistency without changing core functionality.

recommendations.description: Fix the logic error in initDb() at line 9. The statement 'if(db) db;' does nothing and allows re-initialization on subsequent calls, potentially causing race conditions. Change to 'if(db) return;' to properly guard against re-initialization.

Standardize error handling across all database operations. Currently addTodo silently fails, toggleTodo propagates errors, and getTodos has no error handling. Extract an executeWithErrorHandling() wrapper function used consistently across all mutation functions.

Add comprehensive input validation to all database mutation functions. Validate that text parameters are non-empty strings and id parameters are positive numbers. Create validateTodoText() and validateTodoId() helper functions.

Replace '@ts-ignore' comment and 'any' type annotations with proper TypeScript types. Create DBInstance type alias and use it throughout the module to maintain type safety when working with NeverChangeDB.

Create a getDb() helper function that ensures database is initialized before access and throws a clear error if initDb() hasn't been called. Use this throughout all exported functions to prevent null reference errors.

Create comprehensive test suite with minimum 40+ test cases covering: initDb() initialization logic including the early return bug, all CRUD operations, error paths, edge cases (empty strings, negative IDs), database initialization requirements, and migration execution.
Extract MIGRATIONS array as a module-level constant outside initDb() function. This improves testability, makes migration versioning strategy clearer, and allows easier modification of migrations.
Replace console.log and console.error calls with proper logging framework (e.g., Winston, Pino, or the application's configured logger) for better log level control and monitoring integration.
